definitions.explanation: A fire made outdoors, typically for warmth, cooking, burning waste, or enjoyment. Associated with camping, autumn activities, and traditional Japanese winter scenes.

examples.japanese: キャンプ{場|じょう}で{焚|た}き{火|び}を{囲|かこ}んだ。
examples.english: We gathered around the campfire at the campsite.

examples.japanese: {焚|た}き{火|び}で{焼|や}き{芋|いも}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: We made roasted sweet potatoes over the bonfire.

examples.japanese: {住宅地|じゅうたくち}では{焚|た}き{火|び}が{禁止|きんし}されている。
examples.english: Open fires are prohibited in residential areas.

notes:
ORTHOGRAPHY:
Can also be written as {焚火|たきび} or たき{火|び}.

COLLOCATIONS:
・{焚|た}き{火|び}をする - to make a bonfire
・{焚|た}き{火|び}を{囲|かこ}む - to gather around a fire
・{焚|た}き{火|び}{台|だい} - fire pit/fireplace for camping
・{焚|た}き{火|び}を{消|け}す - to put out a fire

CULTURAL NOTES:
{焚|た}き{火|び} is associated with nostalgic winter scenes in Japan. The famous children's song 「たきび」(1941) describes warming oneself by a fire with roasted sweet potatoes. However, open burning is now restricted in many urban and residential areas due to fire safety and air pollution concerns.
